mainText: This is Dose of Good for Tuesday, November 10. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Brazilian scientists turn landfill leachate into fertiliser as good as the commercial kind. Unicamp researchers recovered potassium, nitrogen and phosphorus-rich minerals from a Campinas landfill. In lettuce trials the fertiliser matched or beat commercial NPK, with no detectable heavy metals. Second: Portugal's last circus elephant starts a new life in a sanctuary. Julie, captured in Africa 40 years ago, swapped the ring for 400 hectares in the Alentejo. In just over three months at the Pangea sanctuary she has gained about 100 kg. Third: 12-year-old ballerina from a Rio favela wins a scholarship to dance in the US. Fernanda Rosa won a full scholarship to the Oklahoma Ballet School after performing at YAGP Brazil. She trains at ViDançar, a project serving over 400 people in the Maré favelas. Fourth: Cell therapy gives stiff person syndrome patients their lives back. A Mayo Clinic study using CAR-T cells brought marked improvement: some patients regained daily independence and even returned to work. It is the rare disease Celine Dion has; doctors are still checking whether the gains last. Fifth: Couple gives A$120 million to protect Australia's wildlife. Alexandra and Julian Burt split the gift among 10 conservation groups. It could let the Australian Wildlife Conservancy manage 5% of the country's land. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
